# omni_machine_join_config (Data Source)

Returns what a machine needs in order to register itself with this Omni instance: a partial Talos machine configuration and the equivalent kernel arguments, both carrying a join token.

It is how a machine booted from a stock Talos image joins Omni without Omni-specific installation media. Pass `config` as the machine configuration (user data on a cloud, an `--config` document on bare metal), or `kernel_args` on the kernel command line when booting over PXE or when the platform takes a command line rather than a config. The two are alternatives, not a pair.

It is the Terraform equivalent of `omnictl jointoken machine-config` and `omnictl jointoken kernel-args`.

Everything returned by this data source embeds the join token, so every output is marked sensitive. Writing any of it somewhere readable, a boot script or a CI log, hands the ability to join this instance to whoever can read it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "omni_join_token" "fleet" {
  name       = "fleet"
  expiration = "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}

# What a machine needs in order to register itself with Omni. The partial machine configuration and
# the kernel arguments are two ways of delivering the same thing, so pick whichever the platform
# booting the machine accepts.
data "omni_machine_join_config" "fleet" {
  token_id = omni_join_token.fleet.id
}

# Selecting the token by name instead keeps the secret out of the configuration entirely. Use
# `initial` for the token Omni bootstrapped itself with.
data "omni_machine_join_config" "by_name" {
  token_name = "fleet"

  depends_on = [omni_join_token.fleet]
}

# With neither selector, the instance default is used, which `omni_default_join_token` sets.
data "omni_machine_join_config" "default" {}

# A machine cannot reach Omni's SideroLink UDP port from everywhere. Behind a proxy or a firewall
# that passes only HTTPS, tunnel the WireGuard traffic over gRPC instead. It costs throughput, so
# leave it off where plain UDP works.
data "omni_machine_join_config" "tunnelled" {
  token_id        = omni_join_token.fleet.id
  use_grpc_tunnel = true
}

# Labels to put on every machine that joins with this config. They are signed into the join token,
# and Omni copies them onto the machine when it registers. A label unique to one machine is how to
# find that machine in Omni afterwards, see `omni_machine_wait`.
data "omni_machine_join_config" "labelled" {
  token_id = omni_join_token.fleet.id

  machine_labels = {
    "terraform/machine" = "worker-0"
    "zone"              = "rack-a"
  }
}

# --- Cloud: a stock Talos image plus the join config as user data ---------------------------------
#
# No Omni-specific installation media is needed here. The machine boots a stock Talos image, the
# join config makes it register, and Omni installs whatever schematic the cluster calls for
# afterwards. That costs one install and reboot after the machine joins, and it cannot supply an
# extension the machine needs in order to boot or to reach Omni in the first place: for those, build
# media with `omni_installation_media_preset` instead.
resource "aws_instance" "worker" {
  ami           = data.aws_ami.talos.id
  instance_type = "m5.large"

  user_data = data.omni_machine_join_config.fleet.config
}

# --- PXE: the kernel arguments on the command line ------------------------------------------------
#
# `kernel_args_cmdline` is the same values already joined with spaces, which is what an iPXE script
# or a hypervisor's boot arguments field wants.
resource "local_file" "ipxe" {
  filename = "${path.module}/boot.ipxe"

  content = <<-SCRIPT
    #!ipxe
    kernel vmlinuz ${data.omni_machine_join_config.fleet.kernel_args_cmdline}
    initrd initramfs.xz
    boot
  SCRIPT
}

# --- Proxmox: the config as a cloud-init user data snippet ----------------------------------------
resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_file" "join_config" {
  content_type = "snippets"
  datastore_id = "local"
  node_name    = "pve"

  source_raw {
    file_name = "talos-join.yaml"
    data      = data.omni_machine_join_config.fleet.config
  }
}

# Everything this data source returns embeds the join token, so every output is sensitive. A plain
# `output` of any of it would be refused unless marked as such, and writing it to a file or a log
# hands the ability to join this instance to whoever can read it.
output "join_kernel_args" {
  value     = data.omni_machine_join_config.fleet.kernel_args_cmdline
  sensitive = true
}

# Omni's machine API URL with the token attached, for the places that want the join URL on its own
# rather than a whole command line.
output "omni_endpoint" {
  value     = data.omni_machine_join_config.fleet.omni_endpoint
  sensitive = true
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `machine_labels` (Map of String) Labels to put on every machine that joins with this configuration. They are signed into the join token, so a machine cannot alter them, and Omni copies them onto the machine when it first registers. From then on they are ordinary user labels that can be edited or removed in Omni. A label unique to one machine is how to find that machine once it has joined, see `omni_machine_wait`. Keys under the `omni.sidero.dev/` prefix are reserved. The labels travel on the kernel command line, so the encoded token, labels included, is limited to 1024 bytes.
- `token_id` (String, Sensitive) The join token to embed, i.e. the `id` of an `omni_join_token`. Mutually exclusive with `token_name`; with neither, the instance default is used, which `omni_default_join_token` sets.
- `token_name` (String) Looks the join token up by its `name` instead of its value, which keeps the token out of the configuration. Use `initial` for the token Omni bootstrapped itself with, which has no name of its own.
- `use_grpc_tunnel` (Boolean) Tunnel the SideroLink WireGuard traffic over gRPC instead of sending it as UDP. Needed where the machine cannot reach Omni's SideroLink UDP port, for instance behind a proxy or a firewall that passes only HTTPS. It costs throughput, so leave it off where plain UDP works.

### Read-Only

- `config` (String, Sensitive) The partial Talos machine configuration that joins the machine to Omni, as YAML. It is a fragment rather than a whole configuration: Omni sends the rest once the machine has registered.
- `join_token` (String, Sensitive) The join token that was actually used, resolved from `token_id`, `token_name` or the instance default.
- `kernel_args` (List of String, Sensitive) The same thing as kernel arguments, for booting a machine that takes a command line rather than a configuration. A list, in the order Omni returns them; `kernel_args_cmdline` is the same values already joined.
- `kernel_args_cmdline` (String, Sensitive) `kernel_args` joined with spaces, ready to append to a kernel command line in an iPXE script or a hypervisor's boot arguments field.
- `omni_endpoint` (String, Sensitive) Omni's machine API URL with the join token attached as a query parameter, which is what the `siderolink.api` kernel argument carries, including the gRPC tunnel setting when `use_grpc_tunnel` is set. Useful where something needs the join URL on its own rather than a whole command line. Equivalent to `omnictl jointoken omni-endpoint`.
